summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase ship loop for GSD Phase 66 (API schema cutover + publish gate + tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit CLI → conventional-commit reword → ship → resolve PR reviews.
summary.outcome: All pre-ship gates completed (Verify PASS, Secure SECURED 17/17, Validate Nyquist-compliant, Simplify, SDK E2E 5/5 green, CodeRabbit 15 findings triaged); 5 commits landed. Ship step not yet reached — transcript ends after validation commit.

repo: Phase 66 deleted all 5 shares spec files during the descriptor-ref model cutover without rewriting them, leaving the shares module with zero unit coverage until the Nyquist gate caught it.
89 tests across 11 sdk-e2e suites are pre-existing `describe.skip` quarantines tagged `D-01: SDK runtime stubbed mid-milestone, re-enable at phase 63-65` — not regressions.
GSD secure-phase and validate-phase enforcement hooks are disabled in config; the workflow gates still need to run directly when ship-phase requires them.
The pre-commit hook blocks commits if `openapi.json` has unstaged real changes after `pnpm api:generate`; validation-only DTO changes (e.g. @Matches regex) do not surface into the OpenAPI spec.
`pnpm api:generate` runs a repo-wide eslint pass that triggers prettier on unrelated files (migration files, landing/.astro types) — those diffs must be reverted to keep commit scope tight.
The `landing/.astro/types.d.ts` lint error is a pre-existing issue in a gitignored generated file, not introduced by this phase.
`UpdateEncryptedKeyDto` (shares/dto) and `shares/types.ts` became dead files when the encrypted-key endpoint and service method were removed in this phase.
All sibling IPNS controller endpoints (publish/batch/unenroll/resolve) carry `@Throttle`; the new tombstone endpoint was the only one missing it.
CodeRabbit independently corroborated the security auditor's T-66-E1 write-authority escalation finding.

code.finding: T-66-E1 security bug: minted Share.writeDescriptorRef was set from claimer dto.writeDescriptorRef without checking invite.writeDescriptorRef — a read-only invite could yield a write grant if the claimer supplied a writeDescriptorRef. Fixed by gating on invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null.
Stale comment referencing old FolderIpns entity; removed. The `_publicKey?` param in the private `upsertIpnsRecord` method was also unused (single caller never passed it); removed safely.
tombstone endpoint was missing @Throttle decorator; all sibling destructive endpoints have it. Added to match the established pattern.
rootIpnsName used loose regex /^k[a-z0-9]+$/ instead of the canonical k51qzi5uqu5…|bafzaa… pattern used by sibling DTOs (resolve, tombstone). Tightened.
Same loose IPNS regex as create-share.dto — tightened to canonical pattern for consistency.
psql helper calls lacked statement_timeout; added connect_timeout=5 and options='-c statement_timeout=8000' to both helpers to prevent test hangs.

workflow: Adversarially verify subagent results: confirm auditor-authored spec files test the actual invariant (read `toBeNull()` assertion), confirm no impl files were modified, then run the spec yourself.
After `api:generate`, diff openapi.json semantically (jq-canonicalize + diff) before committing — formatting churn with no semantic change should be reverted.
CodeRabbit CLI can fail on first run with a service connection error; retry immediately — the second run connects fine.
CodeRabbit streams findings in batches; wait for exit 0 and grep the full output before triaging — final count (15) was 5× the first-batch count (3).
When a phase deletes module spec files, the Nyquist gate will surface the gap — author a focused security-critical spec now and defer the full coverage rewrite as a todo rather than blocking ship.
Run `git log --oneline -1` to verify a commit landed; the GSD commit helper can report `commit_failed` while the commit actually succeeded.

friction: CodeRabbit CLI service connection error on first run required a retry before getting any findings.
`pnpm api:generate` reformatted the ApiSchemaCutover migration file and produced openapi.json churn — both required manual `git restore` to keep commit scope clean.
CodeRabbit streamed findings across 3 separate read passes (3 → 9 → 15 findings), requiring repeated output polling rather than a single complete result.
Phase deleted all 5 shares specs without rewriting them; discovering this mid-Nyquist gate added an unplanned spec-authoring subtask before validation could complete.
GSD enforcement hooks (secure-phase, validate-phase) are disabled in project config, so the workflow skills return early — required running auditors directly rather than through the standard gate.
